chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, three women came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so one of them said, 'My husband does not eat meat,' and the other said, 'My husband does not smell perfume,' and the third said, 'My husband does not approach women.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out dragging his robe until he ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'What is the matter with a group of people from my companions who do not eat meat, nor smell perfume, nor approach women?'
Indeed, I eat meat, I smell perfume, and I approach women. So whoever shows preference for my Sunnah, he is from me.

key_terms.يَقْرَبُ: approaches (in the context of marital relations)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say about companions who abstained from meat, perfume, and marital relations?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s rejection of asceticism (zuhd) that leads to neglecting natural human instincts, specifically citing the abstention from meat, perfume, and marital intimacy. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet’s Sunnah is the balanced middle path, where enjoying permissible pleasures is an act of worship rather than a distraction. The narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the balance between spiritual devotion and physical well-being in Islamic practice.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Abu Dawood Al Mustaraq, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Three women came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so one of them said, ‘My husband does not eat the meat’, and the other one said, ‘My husband does not smell the perfume’, and the other one said, ‘My husband does not go near the women’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went out dragging his<sup>saww</sup> robe until he<sup>saww</sup> ascended the Pukpit. So he<sup>saww</sup> Praised Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extolled Him<sup>azwj</sup>, then said: ‘What is the matter with a group of people from my<sup>saww</sup> companions who are neither eating the meat, nor are the smelling the perfume, nor are they going to the women?

But, I<sup>saww</sup> eat the meat, and I<sup>saww</sup> smell the perfume, and I<sup>asws</sup> go to the women. So the one who turns away from my<sup>saww</sup> Sunnah, so he is not from me<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from abu Dawud al-Mustariq from certain persons of his people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Three women came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and one of them said, “My husband does not eat meat.” The other one said, “My husband does not smell perfume.” The other one said, “My husband does not go near the woman.”

The Messenger of Allah came out while his gown dragged behind him until he climbed on the pulpit, praised Allah and glorified Him; then said, “What has happened to certain people of my companions who do not eat meat, smell perfume and do not go near women.
I however, eat meat, smell perfumes and go to women, thus, those who disregard my Sunnah are not of my people.’””
